# GEMMA

## Role

GEMMA is a command-line toolkit for genome-wide efficient mixed-model analysis.
It provides univariate and multivariate linear mixed models, Bayesian sparse
linear mixed models, relatedness-aware association testing, variance-component
estimation, and genotype-by-environment tests.

## simitall Position

GEMMA is the preferred external mixed-model suggestion for moderate-scale animal
or human quantitative-trait studies when the user requests GEMMA, PLINK/BIMBAM
inputs, LMM/mvLMM/BSLMM, or a command-line relatedness-aware benchmark. It is
not automatically the best choice for every animal or human dataset.

## Inputs

- PLINK binary or BIMBAM-style genotype inputs, phenotype, marker annotation,
  covariates, and a compatible relatedness/kinship matrix.
- Genome build, phenotype type, sample QC, and structure/relatedness strategy.

## Outputs and Validation

- Kinship matrix, association result files, model diagnostics, and method
  manifest; SimItAll should add standard plots and synthetic-truth recovery.
- For simulation, compare p-values and recovered loci against retained causal
  truth using harmonized QC and covariates across methods.

## Guardrails

- GEMMA is species-agnostic; its suitability depends on study design, sample
  size, phenotype model, genotype format, and computational constraints.
- Large human binary-trait studies may need tools designed for severe case-control
  imbalance or biobank scale; do not claim GEMMA is the universal human default.
- Preserve covariates, genome build, and relatedness provenance.

## Documentation Provenance

Curated from the official GEMMA manual/repository and Zhou and Stephens (2012).
The official repository notes that active development moved to PanGEMMA in late
2024; verify the current executable/version before running an external command.
